title: The A-U-G-H Team
kidRule: Four letters, A-U-G-H, work as one team! Most of the time the team says '/aw/' and its G and H stay quiet, as in CAUGHT and TAUGHT. In a few words, like LAUGHTER, the same team says '/af/' instead!
hint: A team of four letters is hiding in this word, and it starts with A-U. Can you finish the team?
reminder: The team here is A-U-G-H: A, U, then G and H.

check.question: Which letters spell the '/aw/' sound in CAUGHT?
check.correctAnswer: The team A-U-G-H, with a quiet G and a quiet H!
distractors: The letters O-U-G-H, as in bought
The letters A-W, as in claw

words.def: Took hold of something that was moving, like a ball flying through the air.
words.sent: I caught the ball with one hand.
words.story: A frog's sticky tongue is so quick that a bug is caught in less time than it takes you to blink!
words.card: I *caught* a flying *cau*liflower in my baseball glove!

words.def: Showed or helped someone learn something.
words.sent: My grandpa taught me how to whistle.
words.story: A gorilla named Koko was taught to use about 1,000 hand signs to tell people what she wanted and how she felt!
words.card: The parrot was *taught* to say '*ugh*' whenever it saw broccoli!

words.def: The happy sound people make when something is funny.
words.sent: The room filled with laughter when the clown fell over.
words.story: Rats make tiny chirps of laughter when they are tickled! The sound is too high for our ears to hear.
words.card: The barn burst into *laughter* when the cow began to *laugh* like a duck!

words.def: A girl who is the child of your son or your daughter.
words.sent: Grandma showed her granddaughter how to bake bread.
words.story: Queen Elizabeth II was the great-great-granddaughter of Queen Victoria!
words.card: The queen gave her *granddaughter* a *grand* piano made of cheese!

words.def: Cheeky behavior that breaks the rules.
words.sent: The kitten's naughtiness left paw prints all over the table.
words.story: Long ago, 'naughty' meant having naught, which means having nothing at all. Only later did it come to mean behaving badly!
words.card: The *tin*y puppy's *naughtiness* covered the whole kitchen in flour!

words.def: Acting as if you are better than everyone else.
words.sent: The haughty cat would not even look at the new kitten.
words.story: This word comes from the French 'haut', which means high. A haughty person acts 'high and mighty'!
words.card: '*Ha*!' said the *haughty* peacock, right before he tripped over his own tail!

words.def: Showed someone how to do something one more time.
words.sent: The coach retaught us how to tie our skates.
words.story: The little word part 're-' at the front comes from Latin and means 'again'. You can find it in redo, refill, and replay too!
words.card: I *retaught* my goldfish the sec*ret* handshake!

words.def: So silly or so wrong that it makes you want to giggle.
words.sent: My first try at juggling eggs was laughable.
words.story: A bird in Australia called the kookaburra has a call that sounds just like a person laughing out loud!
words.card: The t*able* wore a *laughable* little hat to dinner!

words.sent: Mia was distraught until she found her kitten asleep under the bed.
words.story: This word began long ago as another form of 'distracted'. Both meant having your mind pulled in different directions!
words.card: The *distraught* dragon had dropped his *str*awberry ice cream!

words.def: A great rush of many things coming at you all at once.
words.sent: The bakery was not ready for the onslaught of hungry customers.
words.story: This word sailed into English from Dutch about 400 years ago. The Dutch word was 'aanslag'!
words.card: An *onslaught* of ballo*on*s filled up the whole bathtub!
